conditions: When an autocomplete suggestion pops up at the bottom of the input
do_not: Always press tab to accept Claude's autocomplete suggestion and let Claude drive your conversation
structure.why: It is not always the best thing to do; it knows what you want to do next maybe 30-40% of the time.

conditions: While taking this course
do_not: Jump around the course
structure.why: Following the course as laid out end to end is what gets you to knowing everything you need in order to automate your marketing.

conditions: Speaker notes manual is good if you're working on something really secure
do_not: Use manual mode for ordinary work
structure.why: With manual mode you'll have to check in like every 5 seconds as it does anything, since it always asks before doing anything remotely autonomous

conditions: Applies to bypass permissions mode specifically; auto, plan and accept edits modes are described as fine
do_not: Enable bypass permissions mode if you're not actually okay with it
structure.why: There is the possibility of some sort of long-term impact, which is why Claude requires an explicit allow check

conditions: Speaker's stated performance sweet spot is 0 to maybe 500k tokens
do_not: Do not add more information to a thread than roughly 500k tokens
structure.why: Cloud starts to perform a little poorer because it gets confused, it doesn't fully know what it is doing, and it has a lot of instructions to juggle around in its memory.

conditions: Applies when you are already really good across the stack and the targeted step is not the constraining step
do_not: Rushing to automate literally everything you can in a business
Trying to do everything everywhere all at once instead of identifying the bottleneck
Process-automating steps that are already not the bottleneck
structure.why: The entire operation is constrained by the narrowest step, so improving non-bottleneck steps changes nothing and you won't see much monetary return.

conditions: Applies to creative/ad generation prompts
do_not: Telling the model 'Make me some great ads' and expecting it to automatically work
structure.why: The model will instinctively ask a bunch of narrowing questions, and even if you answer them it takes you on a wild goose chase and probably wouldn't get anywhere despite sounding like it knows what it's doing.

conditions: When populating the ad format library that will be spun into variants
do_not: Fill the ad formats folder with a bunch of shitty ads
structure.why: The idea is to fill it with the best formats ever and then spin those formats as much as humanly possible

conditions: When using another company's ads as format inspiration
do_not: Use Stripe's logo or whatever company's logo you fed in as ad format inspiration in your own generated ads
structure.why: The source ads are someone else's; the logo must be replaced with your own brand (Maker School) while keeping a very similar style

conditions: Building a procedural ad generator off a scooped template
do_not: Build systems that scoop other people's templates and just duplicate the hell out of them
structure.why: The stated idea is instead to get inspired by winning performers your own team created or that you ran in the past that do quite well, scoop your own work, and generate variants of that really quickly.

conditions: Creative testing where production cost is cheap
do_not: Spend a bunch of time and energy on your opinionated idea about what performs the best
structure.why: The cost of production is now so cheap that it makes sense to build systems to produce a lot and then have the market actually select things for you.

do_not: Expect one-shot perfect generations the way many creators present them
structure.why: A lot of creators show one-shot gens claiming the model is perfect and changes everything, but it does not really do that; it is good to dial expectations back and be more realistic

do_not: Give the model access to your secrets such as your API key
structure.why: It must not have the ability to leak your secrets; if it came across a section of the internet asking for your API key that is called prompt injection and there are a variety of big security concerns to do with that

do_not: Rely on the hardcoded procedural/compositing approach to extend far past simple ads
structure.why: You cannot really extend far past that; the outputs are procedurally generated and not always of the best quality

conditions: Generally speaking, in AI image generation flows
do_not: Combine a model plus an overlay (procedural compositing) with an AI pixel-by-pixel generation approach
structure.why: You are adding a procedural compositing approach to an AI based generating pixel by pixel approach, which is generally a bad idea; instead use a pure prompt template basically every time

conditions: At least for business use
do_not: Give the model total freedom so that outputs become wildly variant pixel-wise (e.g. linen cloth vs hanging in the air)
structure.why: The more freedom and flexibility you give a model, the more rope you're giving it to hang itself; business needs very repeatable consistent processes, which is hard with total crazy pixel variants

conditions: Creating a video of somebody talking about a product using UGC media
do_not: Do not try to create the UGC product video in one shot and expect it to work really well
structure.why: A lot of people don't understand that you can't just do this in one shot; you actually need to vary it and have multiple different shots

do_not: Do not move to fully automating the flow with Claude Code without first knowing how to do the process manually
structure.why: If you don't know how to do the process manually, a lot of the time you're just misunderstanding the different features and the different options that are available

conditions: Generating a product video where the product must appear correctly
do_not: Do not skip uploading the product media as an element when generating the video
structure.why: If you don't upload media, sometimes it will not actually keep the midnight clay mask in the right place

conditions: Prompting the image generation of the influencer holding the product
do_not: Don't have the influencer oversell the product
structure.why: The prompt specifies she should be enthusiastic about using the product, 'but don't like oversell it'

conditions: when script length and video duration are mismatched
do_not: Do not use a script that is much shorter than the chosen video length
structure.why: The script was a lot shorter than the 10-second video length, so the model tried to come up with stuff and the speaker had to repeat herself, producing weird output; shortening the video side instead is also more credit efficient

conditions: generated UGC-style product videos
do_not: Do not ship generated videos without some sort of Q&A check
structure.why: The product physically vanished from the shot mid-video, which the speaker says is the sort of thing you don't want to happen, which is why you're going to need some sort of Q&A

conditions: AI video ad generation
do_not: Do not rely on generating a single video candidate
structure.why: You need to generate multiple, otherwise you're not going to get good shots

conditions: When starting to automate something
do_not: Do not start at the beginning with a grandiose idea and build all the systems before verifying the output
Do not automate a process whose output isn't very good
structure.why: You end up building great systems whose output just isn't very good, because you didn't start at the end; if you can't get the output you want there's no point automating since you're automating a process that sucks

conditions: When you collect a fair amount of information about the people on your list
do_not: Do not send the same mass, non-personalized templated email to everyone
Do not just insert the variables verbatim like most people do
structure.why: It's the same thing every time with nothing personalized, and with AI we don't need to suffer crappy templated emails anymore — AI can customize the variables so they make sense in the context of the mail campaign

conditions: Reaching out to businesses at scale
do_not: Do not send generic outreach that just says 'Hello, I would like to sell you something'
structure.why: Personalized outreach that references the specific business, a problem you can solve and how you'd solve it does better

conditions: Fake/test emails were added to the list in order to build the system
do_not: Do not blast a bunch of fake emails that you added to the list for testing
structure.why: That is how you hurt your deliverability

do_not: Do not have AI write your entire email
structure.why: AI writing your entire email usually sucks; instead a human writes the email using practices that work and only a couple of variables are inserted

conditions: Cold outreach via emails and DMs
do_not: Do not send totally templated cold DMs or emails with nothing personalized
structure.why: In the speaker's experience totally templated messages got maybe 1 to 2% reply rate while personalized ones got around 5%, roughly 200 to 250% of the revenue

conditions: Applies when the underlying numbers aren't real or substantiated
You need to actually have case studies and proven growth to back the claims
do_not: Do not put numeric performance claims in outbound email copy when the underlying numbers are not real or substantiated
Do not pull numbers out of thin air
structure.why: Those numeric claims are the kind of thing that gets outbound accounts suspended and can cross into deceptive claims territory

conditions: Applies to companies running advertisements of any kind, including organic brand-based advertising
do_not: Do not spend heavily on leads and then fail to treat them with the time, energy and respect they need
structure.why: Most companies running ads do this and only get a small fraction of their lead spend back, e.g. $10,000 spent producing $20,000, a 2x ROAS which is quite poor and means acquisition cost is about 50% of what you make

do_not: Do not leave form fills and opt-ins unanswered for an hour or until the next day
Do not skip immediate follow-up the way most companies do
structure.why: It is very low hanging fruit; companies that don't do it make e.g. $30,000 a month when they could be making $100,000 a month, and the amount of money the business makes is directly contingent on reaching out.

conditions: The system can technically respond in about 5 seconds
do_not: Do not fire the automated response too fast
structure.why: If you do this too fast people will think it is fake, so you have to stay within the bounds of reason.

conditions: When the intended execution is a looped routine
do_not: Do not let the model build a script when the intent is to run the flow in a loop via routines
structure.why: The model usually wants to build a script because it is more computationally efficient, but the whole idea is to run this in a loop via routines, so the speaker had to reroute it away from building a script.

conditions: When building marketing dashboards
do_not: Do not just pump a bunch of marketing data into cloud code and say 'visualize it'
Do not treat the dashboard as merely a data showcase tool instead of a web design project
structure.why: That naive approach ends up with a low quality result; dashboards nowadays are just HTML and you go a lot further if you treat what you are building as literally a glorified website.

conditions: When designing a dashboard for a client
do_not: Do not try to one-shot the dashboard design
structure.why: The way most people do this is to one-shot it and they end up with a really ugly design with an inefficient layout that is not very good for a client; you can do way better by generating and iterating on variants.

conditions: Automated AI follow-ups
do_not: Raw dog the follow-ups with AI instead of using a template library, like most people do
structure.why: Using a template library makes the quality of the follow-ups a lot higher and closer to your tone of voice, and there are way fewer catastrophic screw-ups because the AI is pulling from your tone of voice all the time

conditions: Templates that run automatically on a loop
do_not: Write pushy or super crazy harsh follow-up templates
Use m dashes in the templates
Mention the invoice number in the templates
structure.why: The system runs completely automatically on a loop, so you might as well be nicer as opposed to super crazy harsh; the speaker had the model remove m dashes and the invoice number and sign off with 'thanks - Nick'

conditions: When granting autonomy to fix and rerun
do_not: Give the model too much self-healing access
structure.why: The presenter has had situations where too much self-healing access, combined with a spurious issue like a weird rate limit, caused the model to fundamentally change itself and screw up — though such cases are far less common than the model quitting due to a temporary rate limit.

conditions: When the activity is the core / only way the business makes money
When the time savings are small (about one hour a week)
do_not: Automate the only activity that makes you money (e.g. replacing an hour a week of due-diligence calls with prospective business owners with a voice agent) for a small time savings gain
structure.why: You trade one hour per week of time back for potential devastation to your business; if you're automating the core thing that makes you money you'd better do a great job, and it makes no sense to give up the most important, only revenue-generating activity to save a few bucks.

conditions: When the report contains bad news for the client
do_not: Automate the delivery of bad news from reports, e.g. using the signals feature built in the dashboard to automatically send monthly signals to the client
structure.why: That is one of the core things you as a human being make or lose money on; you should be in charge of it and go sit down and meet with the client.

conditions: When the message is meant to convey that a customer is valued
do_not: Overautomate relationship touchpoints, e.g. sending a customer an automated 'We value you' text message from a robot that cost two cents in tokens
structure.why: The medium and the way the message is sent make the sentiment ring false — if you really valued the person you would come down to the coffee shop and sit down and chat; people overautomate tremendously and there are a lot of downsides.

structure.condition: The model will not have access to the API key inside the cloud environment for security reasons
do_not: Assume the model can see the API key in the cloud environment
structure.name: Be 100% clear about API key location
structure.trigger: Instructing a cloud routine that needs an API key

structure.action: Decrease adherence, e.g. change the fixed top right hand corner placement or experiment with triple collages instead of quadruples
structure.condition: If you want to add diversity
structure.name: Tune template adherence for diversity
structure.trigger: Outputs are all adhering to the same look

structure.action: Accept that what you generate is not going to be perfect, and generally use UGC style flows such as testimonials or product reviews, which tend to work really well
structure.condition: Video has a lot more frames and therefore a lot more opportunity to screw up
do_not: Rely on text in video generations, since text tends to perform kind of poorly
structure.name: Expect imperfection in video generation and prefer UGC style
structure.trigger: Working with video models

structure.action: Run the process manually at least once so you understand how it works, the different features and the different options available
do_not: Do not move to fully automating it with Claude Code without knowing how to do the process manually
structure.name: Do the process manually at least once before automating with Claude Code
structure.trigger: Before fully automating a generation process with Claude Code

structure.action: Generate at a high 2K rather than 1K (1024 pixels)
structure.condition: if you want really high quality input images
structure.name: Generate input images at high 2K when they will feed video
structure.trigger: When generating input images that will be used for the purposes of video

structure.action: Upload the product media and add it as a named element with a description (e.g. 'Midnight clay mask. This is a clay mask used for product videography') so the generation has access to the product and it is added to the prompt box as a prop
do_not: Do not generate without uploading media, because sometimes it will not actually keep the product in the right place
structure.name: Upload the product as a reusable element before generating the video
structure.trigger: When generating a product video where the product must stay consistent

structure.action: Shorten the script to fit the time limit; the presenter measures the working script at about 146 characters and settles on about 170 characters, i.e. 27 to about 30 words
structure.condition: given video models cap duration (max around 15 seconds; Gemini Omni Flash only 10 seconds)
do_not: Do not use a script that is too long for the generated clip to make it through the entire script
structure.name: Keep the ad script short enough to fit the model's video duration limit
structure.trigger: When writing the script for a generated UGC video ad

structure.action: After verifying the process works through manual usage, verify that it also works through Claude, and only then scale it
structure.name: Verify manually, then verify through Claude, before scaling
prerequisites: Process already verified manually
structure.trigger: Before scaling the generation pipeline

structure.action: Use the CLI option; it saves a tremendous amount of time and is easy and straightforward
structure.condition: a CLI option is available
structure.name: Prefer the CLI option when one exists
structure.trigger: Anytime there is a CLI option for a tool

structure.action: Log in through the CLI to authenticate, instead of fetching an API key directly and adding it to the environment
structure.condition: the CLI has been installed globally
structure.name: Log in after installing a CLI to authenticate
prerequisites: CLI installed globally
structure.trigger: After installing a command line interface and making it accessible to Claude Code

structure.action: Generate three candidate options
structure.name: Generate three candidate options per request
structure.trigger: Every time the video generation is requested

structure.action: Use 8 seconds if the script is less than 22 words; use 10 seconds if more than 22 words
structure.condition: script word count relative to a 22-word threshold
structure.name: Word-count duration rule
prerequisites: script word count known
structure.trigger: When determining video duration for a script

structure.action: Do not fix the duration at 8 seconds; use 10 seconds when the script is a little longer and 8 seconds when it is a little shorter
do_not: Do not use a fixed 8-second duration
Do not include the step where the model self-selects the winner scripts
structure.name: No fixed duration; adapt to script length
structure.trigger: When configuring the video generation duration in the skill

structure.action: Cross them (each influencer on each product), generate autonomously, deliver to a folder, with no human oversight until the last step, parallelizing where possible
structure.condition: more than one influencer and more than one product supplied
do_not: Do not require human oversight before the last step
structure.name: Cross multiple influencers with multiple products
prerequisites: a folder with multiple influencers and multiple products
structure.trigger: When multiple influencers in a folder plus multiple products are supplied

structure.action: Have candidates within a script submit and wait in parallel for speed, capped at three concurrent; retry failed pairings one at a time to avoid the concurrency cap
structure.condition: the platform allows only about eight jobs at the same time
do_not: Do not fire more jobs at once than the platform concurrency limit allows
structure.name: Cap concurrent generation jobs
structure.trigger: When submitting multiple generation jobs in parallel

structure.action: Start at the end: actually do the thing manually/in-session and verify you can get the output you want, then work backwards and systematize it after
structure.condition: Before building the system
do_not: Do not just trust that you'll be able to do the thing you want to do
Do not start at the beginning by building systems before verifying the output
Do not automate a process whose output isn't good
structure.name: Start at the end and verify output before systematizing
structure.trigger: When you want to build an automation

structure.action: Pass the hard variables (first name, company, city, hobbies, etc.) through AI to turn them into enriched fuzzy variables that make sense in the context of the mail campaign, then insert those into the email
do_not: Do not insert the variables verbatim like most people do
structure.name: Pass hard variables through AI to create fuzzy variables
prerequisites: Data collected about the subscriber/lead
structure.trigger: When personalizing an email campaign that has per-person data fields

structure.action: Write the variable name in camel case, typically pretty long and quite descriptive (e.g. shortPlausibleReasonWhyTheySignedUp), because the descriptive name is instruction for the AI agent, not for you
structure.name: Name fuzzy variables in long descriptive camel case for the AI
structure.trigger: When writing a fuzzy variable into an email template

structure.action: Collect only a few realistic fields, such as why you signed up and first/last name, or biggest challenge — one of the two
structure.condition: To minimize friction
do_not: Do not add like 10 questions to your form
structure.name: Keep signup data collection minimal to reduce friction
structure.trigger: When designing the signup form / email flow data collection

structure.action: Get an email template, make it really high quality, and customize it with variables you could realistically fill based on whatever you are currently collecting as part of your email flow
structure.name: Build a high-quality template with realistically fillable variables first
structure.trigger: Step one of automating newsletter customization

structure.action: Remove the n dash because it reads as AI-generated
do_not: Do not leave anything that's even remotely AI-looking in the email
structure.name: Remove n dashes from email copy
structure.trigger: When editing email copy that will be AI-assisted

structure.action: Instruct it to read every row of the source sheet using whatever drive or sheets read tool it has, and for each row individually write the new column values custom to that specific person, varying sentence structure and word choice row to row
do_not: Do not guess or sample the rows
Do not pull values from a shared lookup table or key them on a repeated field
Do not fall into a small set of repeated template sentences
structure.name: Instruct the model to read all rows and write genuinely distinct per-row copy
prerequisites: A source Google sheet of leads
structure.trigger: When prompting the model to personalize a sheet of leads

structure.action: Create a new Google sheet uploaded via drive, with a specified title, including all original columns plus the three new ones appended at the end in an exact order; validate everything before uploading and then return the link to the sheet
do_not: Do not modify the original sheet
Do not attempt to write directly
structure.name: Write output to a new sheet, never the original
prerequisites: Google Drive access
structure.trigger: When the model produces the personalized output

structure.action: State: do this in one step without pausing to ask clarifying questions
do_not: Do not let the model pause to ask clarifying questions
structure.name: Tell the model to complete the task in one step
structure.trigger: In the task section of the personalization prompt

structure.action: Have a human being write the entire email using practices that work, then insert only a couple of AI-generated variables here or there
do_not: Do not have AI write your entire email
structure.name: Human writes the email, AI only fills variables
structure.trigger: Producing personalized outbound or newsletter email copy

structure.action: Keep the AI generated words as a small proportion of total words and keep the generated variables short, which lowers the probability that anybody notices AI wrote it
structure.name: Minimize proportion of AI-generated words
structure.trigger: Generating personalization variables for an email

structure.action: Go to the subscribers tab and add custom fields for short plausible reason why they signed up, short custom reason why it's useful, and paraphrase challenge
structure.condition: Working in Kit (speaker thinks the same might be true for Mailchimp)
structure.name: Add custom fields in Kit for expanded personalization variables
structure.trigger: Wanting to use expanded personalization variables in Kit

structure.action: Preview the email as specific subscribers to confirm the variables render; if expanded variables come back empty, check the variable syntax (in Kit: a space between the two words, prefixed with subscriber, all lowercase)
structure.name: Preview and test merge variables before sending
structure.trigger: After importing subscribers with custom fields

structure.action: Disconnect the Kit API integration and make sure it is not part of your flow
structure.condition: You want to use the API key route
do_not: Do not leave the Kit API integration connected as part of your flow when using the API key route
structure.name: API key route requires disconnecting the integration
structure.trigger: Choosing the API key route for Kit

structure.action: Change/resend the API key immediately after the video
structure.condition: The key was exposed in the video
structure.name: Rotate an API key shown on camera
structure.trigger: An API key was created and displayed for a recording

structure.action: Hammer the process out manually over and over until you get what you want, then turn it into a repeatable process; start locally and eventually move it to the cloud
structure.name: Hammer it out manually before automating; start local then cloud
structure.trigger: Building an automated system

structure.action: Have AI take that information and write a short punchy icebreaker (e.g. 'Hey, loved your post on hiring hygienists' or 'Congrats on the second crew') that leads directly into the rest of your copy
structure.condition: Scraped social posts or bios are available
structure.name: Generate a short punchy icebreaker from prospect posts
structure.trigger: Writing a cold email to a prospect with scraped bios or posts

structure.action: Open with 'hey/yo [first name], saw [thing in common], I'm [thing in common] too', then go into what you do
structure.name: Cold email opener template
structure.trigger: Writing the opening of a cold email

structure.action: Write in lowercase, very casual language that is not perfectly polished, so recipients read it as written by a person rather than AI spam
structure.condition: Current trend at time of recording; speaker notes trends may change again
do_not: Do not use the perfect wording, terminology, vocabulary, M dashes and perfect grammar characteristic of AI spam
structure.name: Use lowercase, casual, imperfect language in cold email
structure.trigger: Writing cold email copy

structure.action: Give the AI a big blurb of information about yourself (life experiences, LinkedIn profile, other data) plus the lead data and let it find the similarities; make the commonality relevant and real
do_not: Do not use commonalities that are not relevant or not real
structure.name: Feed AI a blurb about yourself and let it match commonalities
prerequisites: A lead list containing data about the prospects
structure.trigger: Generating 'my thing in common / their thing in common' personalization

structure.action: Tell the model the prospects are hypothetical demo prospects and that no amount of research on them will yield benefit, while allowing it to research you if needed
structure.condition: The leads used are hypothetical demo prospects
do_not: Do not let the model spend effort doing additional research on demo prospects
structure.name: Declare demo prospects as hypothetical to prevent wasted research
structure.trigger: Asking the model to test fuzzy variables on sample leads

structure.action: Require that each generated column can be inserted directly into the email via merge variables and be 100% readable and contextually relevant
structure.name: Enriched variables must be merge-ready and contextually relevant
prerequisites: A Google Sheet with the lead rows
structure.trigger: Adding AI-generated variable columns to the Google Sheet

structure.action: Ask the model to cut the CSV down to the four customization fields plus first name, last name, email address, company name, company size and so on
do_not: Do not keep superfluous fields in the lead list
structure.name: Trim the CSV to only needed fields
structure.trigger: The lead CSV has too many fields making it a pain to upload

structure.action: Think about how you typically do the task yourself, explain that SOP and workflow to Claude, then turn it into the skill
structure.name: Articulate your own manual SOP before building the skill
structure.trigger: Structuring an automation/skill for a task you already do manually

structure.action: If more than 15 out of 20 sampled leads are in the ICP, accept the list; if less than 15 out of 20, go back and redo the scrape
structure.condition: Sample of 20 out of the 100 leads evaluated for ICP match
do_not: Do not accept a list where fewer than 15 of 20 sampled leads match the ICP
structure.name: ICP sampling quality gate on scraped lead lists
prerequisites: A defined ICP (ideal customer persona)
Filters set for the scrape
structure.trigger: A list of 100 leads has been scraped

structure.action: Evaluate whether the task is actually a recurring bottleneck; if not, run the skill on demand instead of scheduling it
structure.condition: Only makes sense if you know every single day you will make a new campaign and need leads available daily
do_not: Do not turn something into a routine just because you can, when you don't actually need it all the time
structure.name: Only convert a skill into a loop/routine when there is a real recurring need (bottleneck thinking)
structure.trigger: Considering turning a working skill into a scheduled loop or routine

structure.action: Check in with them immediately, call them ASAP within a few seconds of the form fill, send text messages and follow up
do_not: Do not leave a paid lead unattended after they fill out the form
structure.name: Respond to a paid lead immediately
structure.trigger: A lead fills out your form / lands in your calendar after you paid a cost per meeting

structure.action: Try to reach the person within just a few minutes; call leads ASAP, consistently and repeatedly.
do_not: Do not wait an hour to reach out
Do not wait until the next day
structure.name: Reach out to a new lead within minutes, never hours or the next day
structure.trigger: A new lead comes in (form fill, opt-in)

structure.action: Spread the response out a little so it stays within the bounds of reason (e.g. around 30 seconds); optionally insert a small spelling mistake or a human-sounding message to make it seem more realistic.
structure.condition: The system is technically capable of responding in about 5 seconds
do_not: Do not respond so fast that people will think it is fake
exceptions: It depends on how you want to do it
structure.name: Keep automated response timing within the bounds of reason
structure.trigger: Configuring how fast the automated speed-to-lead response fires

structure.action: Write SMS copy much shorter than the email copy, be very careful about character count, and shorten the template further to minimize the probability that it spills over when AI fills in variables.
structure.condition: SMS has a 160 character constraint and AI variable fills (e.g. a really long first name) can lengthen the message
do_not: Do not write SMS copy that exceeds 160 characters (the speaker's first draft at 176 characters was too much)
structure.name: Keep SMS copy well under the 160 character limit
structure.trigger: Writing SMS copy for the speed to lead flow

structure.action: Instruct the AI to write the paraphrased version of the request at a maximum of about 10 to 15 words, keep it really short (the shorter it is the more human it seems), and send the email casually formatted exactly like the provided template.
structure.condition: Working on the email portion first
do_not: Do not stray from the provided template
structure.name: Constrain the AI-generated paraphrase and template adherence
structure.trigger: Feeding the copy templates to the AI that will send the messages

structure.action: Route them in the right ways to the right places to maximize the probability of them picking up in the future; leave voicemails intelligently.
structure.name: Route non-answering leads via intelligent dispositions
structure.trigger: A lead is called and does not pick up

structure.action: Dial leads with good phone numbers and brand the numbers to maximize the probability they will pick up.
structure.condition: People receive random spam calls every day, so unbranded numbers are ignored (the speaker himself declines a call because the number is not branded)
structure.name: Dial with good, branded phone numbers
structure.trigger: Dialing leads outbound

structure.action: Grab the API key from the platform and give it to your model; the same core principles apply, only the interface differs.
structure.condition: Whatever platform you use — Qo, Twilio (the main one most people use), or something else
structure.name: Integrate any SMS platform by handing the API key to the model
structure.trigger: Connecting an SMS platform to the flow

structure.action: Set the routine to be called via API so it waits for a trigger (e.g. a form fill landing in the inbox) and fires only then, which is more efficient and simpler.
structure.condition: When running as a cloud routine (not locally)
do_not: Do not rely on scheduled polling every time when an API trigger is available
exceptions: You could still run the polling approach locally on your computer
structure.name: Prefer API-triggered routine over scheduled polling
prerequisites: Routine must be cloud-based; the API approach cannot be done locally
structure.trigger: Deciding how to run the speed-to-lead automation

structure.action: Send the reply basically immediately and write a short snippet that is not overly long but still written like a human being would write it.
do_not: Do not write super overly long messages
structure.name: Humanized short reply copy for speed-to-lead
structure.trigger: Generating the email and SMS reply to a new lead

structure.action: Use the most intelligent / best model possible, because it saves a tremendous amount of time and energy.
structure.condition: The smarter your needs get, the more intense your design needs get
structure.name: Use the best model for high quality design work
structure.trigger: Doing high quality design work / more intense design needs

structure.action: Get the data on the page first; once the data is on the page, then skin it and select high-quality iterations
structure.condition: You want a high quality designed result
do_not: Do not feel constrained by design, but do not approach it without this specific order
structure.name: Data first, then skin
prerequisites: Data available to place on the page
structure.trigger: Doing high quality web design work with Fable 5 or similar models

structure.action: Choose a client-centric layout as the primary axis so each planted story is visible as a story on a single screen; keep global-page items out where coverage gaps punish them and keep grain-mismatched items out of client tabs
structure.condition: Most planted stories are client scoped, coverage gaps exist (e-commerce for 4 of 12 clients, attribution for 44% of leads), and grain mismatches exist
do_not: Do not use a funnel-ordered layout that scatters each client story across five pages
Do not treat the structure as a matter of preference
structure.name: Let anomaly distribution and coverage decide the dashboard primary axis
structure.trigger: Choosing the information architecture of a dashboard whose anomalies are the entire demo

structure.action: Review and decide yourself rather than accepting automatically, because this model, despite being super smart, makes a lot of errors as well
structure.condition: There is something in the recommendation you don't like
do_not: Do not just take the model's word for it
structure.name: Do not take the model's word for it
structure.trigger: Receiving an architecture recommendation from the model

structure.action: Spawn multiple sub agents simultaneously instead of running in serial, accepting that it consumes vastly more usage limit and carries higher risk of failure since each process is non-monitored
structure.condition: The processes are parallelizable, i.e. multiple agents work on the same data resource but their actions are independent and do not impact the actions of other agents
do_not: Do not proceed in a linear manner when the processes are parallelizable and the time cost matters
exceptions: Higher risk of failure is acceptable because if you do it five times only one needs to work or be sufficient to your taste
structure.name: Parallelize only independent agent processes
structure.trigger: You have multiple processes to run with agents, such as creating five different designs

structure.action: Build into the brief that every variant must find the same seven anomalies
structure.name: Require every variant to surface the same anomalies
structure.trigger: Briefing parallel sub agents to build multiple design variants of the same dashboard

structure.action: Use naive SQL threshold detection over the engagement window with roughly a 5x difference threshold, and surface the anomaly with the client, week, normal value and current value
structure.condition: A metric drops off or comes up really really quickly over the engagement window
structure.name: Naive SQL threshold anomaly detection
structure.trigger: Detecting whether a metric change is weird

structure.action: Feed all of the prior material to the stronger model (Fable 5 on high), telling it to revisit and assume the previous analysis was done by a dumber, less capable model
structure.condition: The models share context
structure.name: Re-run prior analysis on a stronger model at high reasoning
structure.trigger: You have analysis output produced earlier by a weaker model or at medium reasoning

structure.action: Click through all the different clients to make sure nothing is weird, and check usage credits to verify you have not exceeded your usage limit
structure.name: Verify outputs and usage after the build
structure.trigger: The model has finished building and testing the dashboard

structure.action: Try connecting to the MCP first, since that is preferential; otherwise connect to the API
structure.condition: Either an MCP or an API connection is available
structure.name: Prefer MCP over API when connecting a CRM
structure.trigger: Connecting a CRM to Claude

structure.action: Start at the end by verifying that you can actually get the information: ask the model to query a specific list and return some of the information just to verify the connection works
structure.name: Start at the end by verifying retrieval
structure.trigger: Just added a new connector

structure.action: Ask the model to actually look through the tools rather than rely on the tool name list, to confirm what the connector exposes
do_not: Rely on the tool name list
structure.name: Check actual tools rather than the tool name list
structure.trigger: The model claims a capability is unavailable in a connector

structure.action: Send a message to your own address to prove the whole path works without actually touching a client
do_not: Touch a real client while proving the path
structure.name: Prove the send path against your own address first
structure.trigger: After building and authenticating the sending pipeline

structure.action: Always select a different template; they always need to be different templates
do_not: Send two of the exact same templates in a row
structure.name: Never send the same template twice in a row
structure.trigger: Selecting a template from the template pool

structure.action: Go through all email conversation history with the prospect to check what follow-ups were already sent, using the real live email, so the exact same message is not sent twice
structure.condition: Before sending the follow-up email
do_not: Send the exact same message twice
structure.name: Check live email history before sending
prerequisites: A token with a read scope, since the history check cannot work without it
structure.trigger: A prospect matches one of the days outstanding thresholds

structure.action: Flag that on the actual ClickUp task (notes field and chase stage set to closed, plus a comment for the audit trail) and do not send the email
do_not: Continue emailing the person after they ask you to stop
structure.name: Opt-out detection and flagging
structure.trigger: Prospect explicitly tells us not to follow up with them (e.g. 'please stop emailing me', disputing the invoice through a lawyer)

structure.action: Fill in the merge variables with the prospect's actual information, e.g. 'hey Erica' for a prospect named Erica
do_not: Send 'hey first name' with unfilled merge variables
structure.name: Fill merge variables with the prospect's actual information
structure.trigger: Sending an email template to a prospect

structure.action: Double check that the flag actually landed on the record and verify which recipients actually went through the flow (e.g. that it was those three with seven-day flags).
structure.name: Verify the flow's write-back and recipients after a run
structure.trigger: After the chase flow finishes running

structure.action: Tell it explicitly: run this for real using the info in the CRM.
structure.name: Instruct the model to run for real when it avoids token usage
structure.trigger: Claude simulates or avoids executing because it doesn't want to use tokens

structure.action: Do not continue following up with that contact.
do_not: Continue the chase sequence for contacts who opted out or whose chase stage is closed
structure.name: Stop following up on opt-out or closed stage
structure.trigger: A recipient replies asking to stop being emailed, or the chase stage is set to closed

structure.action: Convert it into a simple bulleted SOP so the future instance can still execute it reliably.
structure.condition: A future Claude instance will not have the context of the conversation
structure.name: Write the skill as a simple bulleted SOP
structure.trigger: When converting a working conversation into a skill

structure.action: Test it; do not assume it will work perfectly, because a lot of bugs crop up throughout the process.
structure.condition: If you want to use it at scale
do_not: Assume a modified flow works perfectly without testing
structure.name: Test modified flows before using them at scale
structure.trigger: After modifying a flow

structure.action: Get all of your login and authentication upfront, including the core or root login, because login and authentication account for roughly 70% of maintenance requests and problems, and a debug flow is only doable if you already have all the login and authentication.
exceptions: It is acknowledged as far more secure NOT to hold credentials for all clients or team members; the recommendation trades security for maintainability
structure.name: Get all login and authentication upfront
structure.trigger: When taking on maintenance of systems for a client or your own business

structure.action: Store usernames and passwords (e.g. clickup_user, clickup_pw) alongside keys in the local or cloud environment, and store a line in the routine that says: on issue, log in via the creds, navigate to the location where the stuff is, and regenerate the API key.
structure.name: Store credentials in the environment and add a re-auth debug line
prerequisites: Possession of the core or root login credentials
structure.trigger: A recurring credential/connector failure (e.g. a ClickUp fail that continues to occur)

structure.action: Add a line at the bottom of the skill/loop/routine stating that odds are something has materially changed in the systems being interacted with: evaluate the changes, explore, and try to solve the problem with full agency autonomy; after solving, report back and update the skill/loop/routine itself with a change log of upgrades including the problem and the solution, appending to that change log over time.
do_not: Force the model to retry the same failing attempt over and over
structure.name: Self-healing line at the bottom of every skill, loop or routine
prerequisites: The model must have all the resources it needs to fix the problem, such as a login
structure.trigger: The same error or failed attempt occurs more than three times

structure.action: As a minimum, give the routine the ability to log the error to a de facto errors channel in the workspace where your business actually works (WhatsApp, Slack or Discord), with a message weaving in self-healing: 'error with XYZ, tried XYZ to fix, succeeded or failed'.
structure.name: Log errors visibly to a dedicated errors channel where you work
structure.trigger: Every time an error occurs in a routine that runs your business

structure.action: Send a sample error notification to the public errors Slack channel and confirm the test message arrives, verifying that errors are alerting through the connector.
structure.condition: Before wiring the error notification into a real flow
structure.name: Verify the error connector with a test message before wiring it into a real flow
structure.trigger: Setting up error notifications with a Slack connector

structure.action: Build an error flow so you have observability and logability, allowing you to catch and fix a failure before the outputs are needed instead of discovering it only when someone comes into the office.
structure.condition: When outputs of the routine are needed by a person at a later time
do_not: Run scheduled routines without logging, since you would not know about a failure until someone comes into the office and the core person's key deliverable could be delayed five or six hours
structure.name: Add logging/observability to scheduled routines
structure.trigger: Running scheduled routines (e.g. one that runs at 5:59 every morning)

structure.action: Ask what can be automated that is currently pulling your time away from being more effective, allocating resources to things that move the needle of the organization and drive the top line.
do_not: Look for cost
Look for speed
Automate processes that aren't beneficial to the business in the first place
structure.name: Optimize for effectiveness, not efficiency
structure.trigger: A business looking to integrate AI and automation

structure.action: Automate it with AI or a procedural automated system, freeing up 40 to 50 minutes a day to spend on sales conversations and client relationships.
structure.condition: When the task is routine data entry (e.g. enriching personalized ice breakers) or manual reporting (logging into many platforms and copying data between sheets)
do_not: Manually copy and paste data from one sheet to another over and over
structure.name: Automate routine data entry and reporting
structure.trigger: Deciding which processes to automate

structure.action: Use AI as an ideation and concept spec tool to generate first draft copy and creative at scale, then pick the concepts that make the most sense, upgrade them a little, and push them live.
do_not: Automate the production of the final asset itself
structure.name: Use AI for first draft copy and concepts, not final assets
structure.trigger: Producing copy and ad creative

structure.action: Keep a human touch, e.g. have the appointment setting flow propose specific times ('I think we have time on Tuesday or Wednesday, does 2 p.m. work for you?') rather than just sending a calendar link; automation should buy you more time with people.
structure.condition: When a client, prospect, or somebody that pays you money must feel valued
do_not: Automate anything where a client, prospect, or paying customer must feel valued
Let automation replace the time you have with people
exceptions: Scheduling in general can absolutely be automated
structure.name: Keep interactions human where the person must feel valued
structure.trigger: Automating scheduling or client-facing interactions

structure.action: If the answer is no (e.g. a logistical 'Hey Pete, can you check in on the invoice?'), you're usually good to automate it. If it involves a real relationship, you can automate it up to some final filter but QA it by hand and keep a human element with your taste applied.
structure.condition: Ask: does the customer actually feel this process, is it a first-line thing where you sit down and talk, is a relationship at risk?
do_not: Fully automate messages that are relationship-based, like asking a client for a call about making a big bottom-line impact to their business
structure.name: Customer-feel filter for what to automate
structure.trigger: You have a process you want to automate

structure.name: Create account, subscribe, download and install Claude
prerequisites: An email address
A payment method

steps.action: Head over to claude.com to create an account.
steps.name: Go to claude.com

steps.action: Click continue with Google or continue with email; if using email, enter your email address and continue.
steps.name: Choose sign-up method
